blocks.text: 核心要点

inlines.text: ：Rerank 5 Pro 在主要公开基准测试中领先，而 Rerank 5 Fast 以更低成本提供接近领先水平的性能。
在企业各领域表现强劲
：Rerank 5 在金融、医疗、科学研究、解析文档和多语言检索领域确立了领先地位。
：Rerank 5 新增功能——单次 Rerank 调用即可返回每个文档中最相关的段落，在答案质量损失极小的前提下降低 LLM token 成本。
：跨查询和领域的一致分数让团队可以设定单一阈值，决定哪些内容进入 LLM。
：可通过 Cohere API、Model Vault、Microsoft Foundry、Amazon SageMaker、在您自己的 VPC 或本地私有部署，以及面向所有 North 用户提供。只需几行代码即可开始使用。

blocks.text: 引言
今天，我们发布 Rerank 5，这是我们迄今最先进的企业检索模型，提供 Pro 和 Fast 两个版本。

inlines.text: 今天，我们发布 Rerank 5，这是我们迄今最先进的企业检索模型，提供 Pro 和 Fast 两个版本。

blocks.text: Rerank 5 帮助团队找到正确的信息，将最相关的上下文发送给 LLM，并为客户提供更贴合需求的搜索体验。借助 Rerank 5 Pro，我们在重排序质量上树立了新标准，尤其是在推理密集型搜索、视觉信息丰富的文档和关键企业领域。Rerank 5 Fast 将这一质量带给对延迟和成本敏感的工作负载。两个模型都引入了 Context Focus，可精确定位文档中最相关的文本片段，超越文档级或分块级检索，精准呈现真正重要的信息。

blocks.text: LLM 读取的每个 token 都是您要付费的 token，而检索决定了这些 token 是哪些。随着智能体在更长的文档上执行更多搜索，检索已成为企业控制 AI 成本、延迟和答案质量的关键杠杆。

blocks.text: 性能

Rerank 5 Pro 在 ViDoRe V3、nanoMTEB、BRIGHT 和 BEIR 等公开基准测试中领先——优于所有参与测试的竞争模型。在评估的 46 个复合数据集中，Rerank 5 Pro 在 39 个上排名第一，在 43 个上至少排名第二。模型使用 RCP-nDCG@10 进行评估，这是 Cohere 开发的一种方法，旨在解决传统 nDCG 因相关性判断不完整（qrel 覆盖率）而导致的局限。

blocks.text: 这一优势在 BRIGHT 上尤为明显，该基准测试推理密集型检索，识别相关文档需要超越关键词或语义相似度的更深层理解。Rerank 5 Pro 得分 82.2，比 Voyage AI Rerank 3 高出 5.8 分，比 Rerank 4 Pro 高出 12.4 分，这是它在四项主要基准测试中最大的代际提升。Pro 在 ViDoRe V3 上还以 1.6 分领先最强的外部竞争对手，在 BEIR 上领先 1.8 分，在 nanoMTEB 上领先 3.4 分。这些提升对智能体工作流日益重要，因为复杂、多步骤的查询需要具备推理相关性的能力，并返回可能与原始查询不太相似的证据。

blocks.text: 特定领域表现

blocks.text: 延迟 + 吞吐量
Rerank 5 Fast 专为大规模处理而打造。在持续负载下，Fast 在单块 NVIDIA A100 GPU 上每秒可重排序约 187 篇标准长度文档（1,000 个 token），吞吐量达到 Pro 的 2.9 倍。

inlines.text: Rerank 5 Fast 专为大规模处理而打造。在持续负载下，Fast 在单块 NVIDIA A100 GPU 上每秒可重排序约 187 篇标准长度文档（1,000 个 token），吞吐量达到 Pro 的 2.9 倍。

blocks.text: Fast 的响应时间也比 Pro 快近 3 倍，非常适合对延迟敏感的应用，以及每个任务中需要执行多次搜索的智能体。Pro 仍然最适合那些将排序质量置于速度之上的应用。

blocks.text: 上下文聚焦：释放更智能的 token 经济效益

inlines.text: 上下文聚焦：释放更智能的 token 经济效益

blocks.text: 随着文档变得越来越长，AI 智能体从更多来源检索信息，传递给 LLM 的上下文量持续增加。然而，每篇文档中往往只有少数几句话与查询相关。处理不必要的内容会推高 token 成本、增加延迟，并可能引入噪声，从而降低答案质量。

inlines.text: 随着文档变得越来越长，AI 智能体从更多来源检索信息，传递给 LLM 的上下文量持续增加。然而，每篇文档中往往只有少数几句话与查询相关。处理不必要的内容会推高 token 成本、增加延迟，并可能引入噪声，从而降低答案质量。

blocks.text: 上下文聚焦是随 Rerank 5 推出的全新可选能力，它不仅能识别相关文档，还能精确定位最关键的具体段落。可配置的阈值让开发者能够在减少上下文与保留证据之间取得平衡，而单次 Rerank API 调用即可同时返回文档级相关性分数和带分数的文本片段。应用随后可以只将最相关的证据传递给 LLM，而无需在检索流程中增加额外步骤。

blocks.text: 将上下文与答案质量解耦

inlines.text: 将上下文与答案质量解耦

blocks.text: 我们在 30 个问答数据集上测量了当上下文聚焦移除更多检索文本时答案质量的变化。移除一半上下文仅损失 2 个百分点的答案质量（保留 96%），移除四分之三也仅损失 7 个百分点（保留 87% 的答案质量）。因此，上下文聚焦就像一个调节旋钮：适中的设置几乎不付出代价，而需要更大节省的团队可以用部分质量换取最多 10 倍的上下文缩减。

blocks.text: 随着检索文本被移除时的答案质量。每个模型从同一组 50 个候选中选出前 5 篇文档，然后在一系列阈值下移除文本（每个阈值一个点）：Rerank 5 使用上下文聚焦，基线模型使用各自的压缩器。Qwen3.5-9B 根据剩余内容作答，Qwen3.5-35B 对答案进行评分。x 轴：被移除的检索 token 占比；y 轴：平均评审分数；两者均在来自 ViDoRe、UNICORN、BRIGHT-Pro 和智能体问答的 30 个单轮问答数据集上取平均值（每个最多 500 条查询）。

blocks.text: 随后，我们给一个搜索智能体逐步搭建了一套检索栈，从关键词搜索（BM25）开始。加入 Rerank 5 Pro 后，准确率从 46% 提升到 49%。开启 Context Focus 后，token 用量减少，准确率进一步提升。在默认阈值（0.1）下，每个任务的 token 用量下降了 19%，准确率升至 57%。在 0.4 下，token 用量下降了 34%，在每个数据集上都更低，准确率达到 58%。总体而言，在 Context Focus 设为 0.4 时，完整检索栈比单独使用 BM25 少用 35% 的 token，同时准确率更高（58% 对 46%）。在六个深度搜索基准上，它少用 41% 的 token，准确率从 39% 升至 52%，每个基准在这两项指标上都有改善。​

blocks.text: Rerank 5 的原始分数可读作概率。文档按分数分入十个区间，每条线连接一个模型的各区间：区间的平均分数（横轴）对应其文档被判定为有用的比例（纵轴）。在虚线对角线上，分数恰好等于概率；位于其下方的线高估了相关性，位于其上方的线则低估了相关性。分数按返回原值使用，未重新校准。左图：盲评人工评分员，2,262 份文档；有用 = 在五点量表（Off-topic、Topical、Useful、Answers、Complete）上平均评级为“Useful”或更高。右图：NIST TREC-DL 评估员，20,646 份文档；有用 = 在 NIST 的 0–3 量表上评级为 2（“高度相关”）或更高。

inlines.text: 按相关性过滤，而非按数量。
与其向 LLM 传入固定的 top-k，不如保留所有高于阈值的文档。窄查询会传入少量文档，宽泛查询会传入更多文档，模型看到的噪声更少。
知道何时没有返回相关内容。
如果没有文档达到阈值，智能体可以重写查询或表示不知道，而不是根据排名第一的文档作答。
跨领域和模型规模使用同一阈值。

blocks.text:
#rerank with Context Focus
import os
import requests

query = "How much did card provisions rise in Q3?"

documents = [
    "Market update. Commercial real estate prices fell 6% this year as office "
    "vacancies climbed. Analysts expect refinancing pressure on landlords to "
    "persist into next year.",
    "Q3 credit quality. Net charge-offs held steady at 0.42% of average loans. "
    "Commercial real estate loans stood at $14.3 billion, or 9% of total loans. "
    "Office properties accounted for $2.1 billion of that balance. Card "
    "provisions rose $85 million on higher delinquencies.",
    "Q3 mortgage lending. Residential mortgage originations rose 11% as rates "
    "eased. The average loan-to-value ratio on new lending was 68%.",
]

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.cohere.com/v2/rerank",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CO_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "rerank-v5.0-pro",
        "query": query,
        "documents": documents,
        "top_n": 2,
        "relevant_spans": {"mode": "enabled", "threshold": 0.4, "max_spans": 10}, #toggle Context Focus
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    document = documents[result["index"]]
    print(f"{result['relevance_score']:.2f}  {document[:60]}...")
    for span in result.get("relevant_spans") or []:
        print(f"      {span['score']:.2f}  {document[span['start']:span['end']]}")

blocks.text: Introduction
Today, we're releasing Rerank 5, our most advanced enterprise retrieval models yet, available in Pro and Fast tiers.

inlines.text: Today, we're releasing Rerank 5, our most advanced enterprise retrieval models yet, available in Pro and Fast tiers.

blocks.text: Rerank 5 helps teams find the right information, send the most relevant context to their LLMs, and give customers more tailored search experiences. With Rerank 5 Pro, we’ve set a new standard in reranking quality, especially on reasoning-intensive search, visually rich documents, and key enterprise domains. Rerank 5 Fast brings that quality to latency- and cost-sensitive workloads. Both models introduce Context Focus, which pinpoints the most relevant spans of text within documents, going beyond document- or chunk-level retrieval to surface precisely the information that matters.

blocks.text: Performance

Rerank 5 Pro leads public benchmarks such as ViDoRe V3, nanoMTEB, BRIGHT, and BEIR - outperforming every competing model tested. Of the 46 composite datasets evaluated, Rerank 5 Pro ranked first on 39 and placed at least second in 43. Models are evaluated using RCP-nDCG@10, a Cohere-developed methodology designed to address limitations in traditional nDCG caused by incomplete relevance judgments (qrel coverage).

blocks.text: The advantage is particularly pronounced on BRIGHT, a benchmark testing reasoning-intensive retrieval, where identifying relevant documents requires deeper understanding beyond keyword or semantic similarity. Rerank 5 Pro scores 82.2, outperforming Voyage AI Rerank 3 by 5.8 points and Rerank 4 Pro by 12.4 points, its largest generational gain across the four headline benchmarks. Pro also leads the strongest external competitor by 1.6 points on ViDoRe V3, 1.8 on BEIR, and 3.4 on nanoMTEB. These gains are increasingly important for agentic workflows, where complex, multi-step queries demand the ability to reason about relevance and return evidence that may not closely resemble the original query.

Rerank 5 Fast is built for volume. Under sustained load, Fast reranks about 187 standard-length documents (1,000 tokens) per second on an NVIDIA A100 GPU - delivering 2.9x the throughput of Pro.

blocks.text: Context Focus: unlock smarter token economics

inlines.text: Context Focus: unlock smarter token economics

blocks.text: As documents grow longer and AI agents retrieve information from more sources, the amount of context passed to LLMs continues to increase. Yet, often only a few sentences within each document are relevant to the query. Processing unnecessary content drives up token costs, increases latency and can introduce noise that reduces answer quality.

inlines.text: As documents grow longer and AI agents retrieve information from more sources, the amount of context passed to LLMs continues to increase. Yet, often only a few sentences within each document are relevant to the query. Processing unnecessary content drives up token costs, increases latency and can introduce noise that reduces answer quality.

blocks.text: Context Focus, a new optional capability launching with Rerank 5, goes beyond identifying relevant documents to pinpoint the specific passages that matter most. Configurable thresholds let developers balance context reduction with evidence retention, while a single Rerank API call returns both document-level relevance scores and scored text spans. Applications can then pass only the most relevant evidence to an LLM, without adding steps to the retrieval pipeline.

blocks.text: Decouple context from answer quality

We measured how answer quality varied as Context Focus removes more of the retrieved text across 30 question-answering datasets. Removing half the context sacrificed only 2 percentage points of answer quality (96% retained), and removing three-quarters lost just 7 (87% answer quality retained). Context Focus therefore works like a dial: moderate settings are close to free, and teams that need bigger savings can trade some quality for up to 10x less context.

blocks.text: We then gave a search agent a retrieval stack built up one step at a time, starting from keyword search (BM25). Adding Rerank 5 Pro raised accuracy from 46% to 49%. Turning on Context Focus then cut tokens and raised accuracy further. At the default threshold (0.1), tokens per task fell by 19% and accuracy rose to 57%. At 0.4, tokens fell by 34%, lower on every dataset, and accuracy reached 58%. Altogether, the full stack with Context Focus at 0.4 used 35% fewer tokens than BM25 alone, at higher accuracy (58% vs 46%). On the six deep-search benchmarks, it used 41% fewer tokens, and accuracy rose from 39% to 52%, with every benchmark improving on both measures. ​

blocks.text: Calibrated relevance scores
With Rerank 5, a score of 0.7 now means a 70% chance the document is useful.

inlines.text: With Rerank 5, a score of 0.7 now means a 70% chance the document is useful.

blocks.text: Every reranker returns a relevance score, but until now those scores were mostly good for sorting. What counted as a "good" score changed from model to model. Teams had to tune a cutoff for each model and re-tune it on every upgrade.

inlines.text: Every reranker returns a relevance score, but until now those scores were mostly good for sorting. What counted as a "good" score changed from model to model. Teams had to tune a cutoff for each model and re-tune it on every upgrade.

blocks.text: Rerank 5's scores are calibrated out of the box: the relevance_score returned with each result reads as the probability that the document is useful, with no change to your request or the response format. Pro and Fast also agree on where the line is: "more likely useful than not" is a score of 0.50 for Pro and 0.45 for Fast.

blocks.text: Rerank 5's raw scores read as probabilities. Documents are sorted into ten bins by score, and each line connects a model's bins: the bin's average score (across) against the share of its documents judged useful (up). On the dotted diagonal, a score is exactly a probability; lines below it overstate relevance, and lines above it understate it. Scores are used as returned, with no recalibration. Left: blind human graders, 2,262 documents; useful = a mean grade of "Useful" or higher on a five-point scale (Off-topic, Topical, Useful, Answers, Complete). Right: NIST TREC-DL assessors, 20,646 documents; useful = grade 2 ("highly relevant") or higher on NIST's 0–3 scale.

blocks.text: We checked this against two independent sets of human judgments that no model was trained on: a blind panel of graders and NIST's TREC Deep Learning assessors. On both, Rerank 5 follows the diagonal far more closely than any other reranker. Competing models sit below it, overstating relevance: documents Voyage AI Rerank 3 scored around 0.55 were only 24% useful to the human graders.

blocks.text: The table below sums this up as expected calibration error (ECE): the average gap between a model's scores and the real share of useful documents, where 0 is perfect. Rerank 5's is about 0.06 on both sets of judgments; every other reranker we tested has nearly four times that error or more. Calibration doesn't cost ranking quality, either: Rerank 5 Pro and Fast rank first and second in average precision on both.

blocks.text: Why it matters

inlines.text: Filter by relevance, not by count.
Instead of passing a fixed top-k to your LLM, keep every document above the threshold. Narrow queries pass a few documents, broad ones pass more, and the model sees less noise.
Know when nothing relevant came back.
If no document clears the threshold, an agent can rewrite the query or say it doesn't know, instead of answering from whatever ranked first.
One threshold across domains and model sizes.
Across BRIGHT, NanoBEIR, and ViDoRe V3, the default stays between 0.47 and 0.53 for Pro, and Pro and Fast are within 0.05 of each other.

blocks.text:
#rerank with Context Focus
import os
import requests

query = "How much did card provisions rise in Q3?"

documents = [
    "Market update. Commercial real estate prices fell 6% this year as office "
    "vacancies climbed. Analysts expect refinancing pressure on landlords to "
    "persist into next year.",
    "Q3 credit quality. Net charge-offs held steady at 0.42% of average loans. "
    "Commercial real estate loans stood at $14.3 billion, or 9% of total loans. "
    "Office properties accounted for $2.1 billion of that balance. Card "
    "provisions rose $85 million on higher delinquencies.",
    "Q3 mortgage lending. Residential mortgage originations rose 11% as rates "
    "eased. The average loan-to-value ratio on new lending was 68%.",
]

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.cohere.com/v2/rerank",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CO_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "rerank-v5.0-pro",
        "query": query,
        "documents": documents,
        "top_n": 2,
        "relevant_spans": {"mode": "enabled", "threshold": 0.4, "max_spans": 10}, #toggle Context Focus
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    document = documents[result["index"]]
    print(f"{result['relevance_score']:.2f}  {document[:60]}...")
    for span in result.get("relevant_spans") or []:
        print(f"      {span['score']:.2f}  {document[span['start']:span['end']]}")
